race_context: The School City of Hobart serves most of the city of Hobart in Lake County and runs six schools: Hobart High School, Hobart Middle School, three elementary schools (Joan Martin, Liberty and Veterans at Mundell) and the Early Learning Center at George Earle {wiki_hobart}{hob_buildings}. Enrollment was 4,088 in 2019–20, the latest district-wide figure this guide found {wiki_hobart}. Dr. Peggy Buffington is superintendent {hob_supt}.

The board has seven members, all elected at large: four seats were filled in 2022 and three in 2024 {lc_results_2022}{lc_results_2024}{hob_board}. The current members are President Rikki Guthrie, Vice President Sandra J. Hillan, Secretary Frank Porras, Donald H. Rogers, Stuart B. Schultz, Bradley Keehn and David Kostbade {hob_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: four at-large seats. The county's sample ballot reads 'Vote for not more than Four (4),' not one as the state list shows {lc_sample_ho02}{in_list}. The four candidates are the four incumbents elected in 2022: Guthrie, Hillan, Rogers and Schultz {lc_sample_ho02}{lc_results_2022}. With four candidates for four seats, the race is uncontested.
Not on this ballot: Porras, Keehn and Kostbade, who ran unopposed for three at-large seats in 2024 {lc_results_2024}.

Budget and SEA 1 (2025): in September 2025 the Post-Tribune reported that the board had approved an engagement letter with the financial adviser Stifel, Nicolaus & Co. to advise on possible bond refunding and other relief from circuit-breaker (tax-cap) losses, and that the district was retaining Policy Analytics LLC to forecast future tax revenue {posttrib_sea1}. The paper reported that Hobart already loses about 80% of its tax levy to the property-tax caps, and quoted Buffington describing SEA 1 as a second circuit breaker: 'We have to engage with our financial planners to be able to look at the devastation the legislation did' {posttrib_sea1}.

Operating referendum (2017 and 2025): voters first approved an eight-year operating levy of up to 24.6 cents per $100 of assessed value in November 2017 {dlgf_hob_2017}{dlgf_hist}. The board's Resolution 2024-39 asked voters to renew the levy at the same rate for 2026 through 2033 {dlgf_hob_res}. On May 6, 2025, voters approved the renewal 1,188 to 274 (81.3%) {lc_results_2025}. The district's spending plan projects about $2.8 million a year, mostly for transportation ($2.7 million) with $75,000 for school safety {dlgf_hob_plan}.

Charter schools (2025): two charter schools, Neighbors' New Vistas High School and Discovery Charter School, chose to share in the referendum revenue, at a projected $13,504 and $2,813 a year {dlgf_hob_res}{dlgf_hob_plan}.
No school referendum on the 2026 ballot: the only public questions on the Hobart sample ballot are two statewide constitutional amendments {lc_sample_ho02}.

Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of the 2026 Hobart race. The district's online board minutes (hosted on ic-board.com) could not be opened, so board decisions in 2025–2026 could not be reviewed {hob_meetings}.
